sources.title: CMOS Low-Power Optical Transceiver for Short Reach
sources.organization_or_authors: R. Yang, Y. Dang, J. Chen, D. Li, F. Svelto
facts: 28 nm CMOS architecture combines equalization/predriving, stacked current reuse and asymmetric high-impedance current steering.
Measured standalone TX: 25 Gb/s NRZ, 850 nm / 14 GHz VCSEL, bias 6 mA, modulation 6 mApp, 39.8 mW, reported 1.59 pJ/bit.
Measured back-to-back link is reported separately at up to 20 Gb/s; Figure 10 is simulated, Figure 19 measured.
does_not_establish: Different process, optical device and energy denominator; not comparable to our pJ/net-bit result without harmonizing boundaries.
No BER qualification is inferred from eye diagrams. B2B and standalone TX results must not be merged.

maturity_inventory.scope: Core only, excludes latest reference/rail/device changes
Core only, excludes latest reference/rail/device changes

interpretation_limits: The listed latest frozen candidates are the prior completed stage; new driver-methods experiments are in progress and not covered by this productization audit.
Historical GDS, LVS and PEX do not transfer to a different transistor inventory, device family, capacitor or rail circuit.
A/B use a fixed 20 um synthetic/dynamic load and optical/RX proxy; VCSEL has a different optical load/RX. These are not a common measured physical link.
Finite-frame E_source+/N_payload is not proven steady-state system energy; startup/capacitor storage and bias settling must be checked.
Zero observed errors in a short deterministic frame do not establish a production BER or MTBF.
Blender visualizations use exaggerated heights/separation and are not field-solver, process simulation or package signoff.

mechanism_hypotheses.reasoning: Lower R reduces an input RC pole; smaller driven MOS can lower gate/diffusion capacitance but raise on-resistance and hurt compliance.
Transient charge transfer is DeltaQ=C*DeltaV; a real source supplies the energy. Pulse shaping can compensate some ISI but cannot eliminate recombination or arbitrary optical loss.

Keeping current available can avoid turning the entire bias branch on/off; static bias remains an energy cost. Reuse/high-impedance outputs trade termination/reflection and headroom against wasted current.
Switched capacitive energy approximately scales with C*V^2; DC dissipation with V*I. Whole-driver energy also includes references, regulation, rail loss and startup.

recommended_gate_sequence: Freeze target net rate, coding overhead, optical budget, allowed current/voltage/temperature, BER target and energy boundary.
Calibrate traceable emitter IV/LIV/CV/S21 versus current and temperature; expose unmeasured parameters as sensitivity ranges.
Complete prelayout PVT/mismatch, longer frames, startup/brownout/fault/disable and steady-energy checks.
Choose provider-accepted full PDK, rule/tool versions, BEOL option, pad/ESD library and package before final floorplan.
Build new full driver/test macro and pad ring; DRC/LVS/ERC/antenna/density/mixed-well review, PEX, timing and supply/reliability checks.
Co-design package/PCB/optical coupling, extraction/reference planes, return paths and test access.
Deliver reviewed manufacturing/assembly/test package; obtain provider acceptance independently of local reports.
Bring up silicon with current-limited power, DC/fault tests then optical LIV/S21/eye/BER and temperature/reliability qualification.
